name: Bé Chuma
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
response: Bé Chuma (Bechuma, Bé Cuma, Bé cuma) Irish goddess or heroine. A woman of Irish legend, one of the magical people called the Tuatha Dé Danann, Bé Chuma was known for her car38 beating the bounds nal appetites. She originally came from the Otherworld, where she left her powerful husband for another man, after which she was banished to this world. There she continued her fickle ways, lusting after her stepson Art Mac Cuinn while married to the king of Tara, Conn of the Hundred Battles.

text: Bé Chuma is an Irish goddess or heroine of the Tuatha Dé Danann. She was known for her strong carnal appetites. She came from the Otherworld, where she left her strong husband behind, and was sent to this world. There she lusted after her stepson Art Mac Cuinn. She married the king of Tara, Conn of the Hundred Battles. Tara's queen stood for the sovereignty of the land, so Bé Chuma could remove one king for another. She left Tara when Art returned with a wife who demanded her exile.
